summary.headline: SBI Life H1 FY27 VoNB rose 19% to INR32.7bn at a 27.9% margin, while PAT grew 17% to INR12.7bn despite a INR5.3bn GST hit.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 showed solid value growth: VoNB up 19% to INR32.7bn with margin of 27.9% (Q2 at 29.3%), and embedded value up 15% to INR873.5bn. Individual rated new business premium grew 12% to INR97.2bn, but management said IRP growth of about 12% in H1 is below the 14-15% full-year target it reiterated. A one-off GST impact of INR5.3bn weighed on profit and opex ratio; excluding it, PAT was INR16.9bn (+39%) and VoNB INR33.8bn (+19.4%). Management said the mix shift toward non-par and annuity products helped margins, while the agency channel slowed in Q2 and the banca channel was softer in September.

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY; private market share 22.6%, total market share 16%
vs 6.2% / 10.9% in H1 FY26; opex ratio ex-GST 5.8%

segments.name: Individual protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR4.3bn, +16%; pure protection +26%; including riders, protection APE +30%. Pure protection share moved from 90:10 to 58:42 versus ROP, and rider attachment is about 49%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group new business premium INR65.3bn (+6%), 32% of NBP; group APE INR117.5bn (+18%); group protection APE INR16bn (+134%). Credit life APE about INR140 crore in H1, roughly flat.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRB)
segments.commentary: Contributes 53% of total APE; individual APE INR59.9bn (+10%). SBI branch productivity INR5 million on individual APE for the period.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR32bn (+12%); non-ULIP share rose from 39% to 47%; agency individual sum assured +50%. Added over 72,000 agents gross; average productivity about INR2 lakh. Q2 growth slowed to about 6%.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, other banks, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 67% and contributed 19% of total APE. Growth driven by a low base and new partners; J&K Bank added as a banca partner. Other-bank channel growing 30%+, mainly non-par.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: ULIP share 62% of product mix versus 65% in H1 FY26. Guaranteed non-par savings INR24.7bn (+27%); annuity and pension NBP INR46.2bn; participating individual APE INR5.1bn (+9%).

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 IRP growth guided at 14-15%, reiterated despite H1 at about 12%; Q3 is seasonally stronger.
VoNB margin guidance of 26-28% maintained for the current half.
Management expects limited impact from IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper and sees SBI Life as among the least impacted insurers; final guidelines awaited.
Plans to launch a regular-pay deferred annuity soon (possibly in Q3), with margin similar to or above company average.
Full-year ULIP share target of about 63%; H1 closed at about 62%.
IFRS 17 transition approach to be finalised by end-March 2027, with adoption from June 30, 2027; investor day planned before that.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: 14 new branches opened in the period.
Agent network: over 72,000 agents added on a gross basis.
Digital: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 71% processed through automated underwriting.
Hedging: 80% of premium hedged per policy; management views 80% as optimal.
demand_pricing: Non-par pricing repriced in Q2 with a pass-through of yield benefits to customers; management says it will keep repricing in Q3 and Q4.
Uniform commission and uniform product pricing across channels, so margins are the same across channels.
Management attributes about 70bps of H1 margin gain YoY to yield curve movement.
Individual sum assured +36% and group sum assured +78%; rider sum assured 40% of individual sum assured.
Persistency at 13th, 25th and 49th months: 87.6%, 78.4% and 69.3%, up 44, 110 and 40bps YoY.
Death claim settlement ratio 99.1%; misselling ratio 0.035%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company satisfied with about 12% IRP growth versus its 13-15% aspiration, and what is the reason for the negative operating-adjustment impact in the VoNB walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 14-15% IRP growth for FY27 and said it is in line with industry growth. The VoNB negative came from a March 2026 assumption refinement (mortality, persistency, expenses), not a change made in the period; operating variances were all positive.

qa_highlights.question: How did banca trend in October and what is the outlook for non-par and annuity distribution across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 is seasonally strong and expected to be higher growth. Products are available across all channels and uniformly priced; the uptick has been stronger in agency than banca, and banca sales of these products are being pushed.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins move higher than the 26-28% guidance, and how much of Q2 margin gain came from non-par?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stick to 26-28% guidance. It does not disclose the non-par margin contribution, but said the mix change helped Q2 margin and that repricing will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI distribution paper, including credit life and bancassurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SBI Life is among the least impacted; credit life attachment is under 50% of the bank portfolio and largely paid via loans. It has little partnership outside SBI, so no challenge is seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did agency growth slow sharply in Q2 and what is the protection mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said agency growth will normalise within a couple of months and the FY27 target is intact. Pure protection moved to 58:42 versus ROP, and the sum assured growth is the highest in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the conservation ratio fall to about 82% from 84%, mainly in linked pensions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is marginal and not a concern; 13th and 25th month persistency improved and renewal collections grew at high double digits.

risks_watch: IRP growth of about 12% in H1 versus the 14-15% full-year target; Q3 must deliver a sharp acceleration.
Final IRDAI distribution guidelines (commission caps, differential pricing), which could affect banca and credit life economics.
IFRS 17 transition approach and treatment of ULIP CSM release, still undisclosed.
Conservation ratio fell to about 82% from 84%, with the largest decline in linked pensions.
Q2 agency slowdown and reliance on the Q3 banca season.
Margin sustainability: Q2 gains partly from yield-curve movements and non-par repricing that may be passed to customers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year growth and margin targets and on regulatory impact, but evasive on quarterly details: it declined to split IRP growth by channel or quantify non-par margin and yield-curve contribution, and deferred the IFRS 17 and ULIP CSM questions.
key_quotes: But at the start of the financial year, we had given a guidance that we'll be growing for the year at around 14% to 15% and we are sticking to our guidance for the entire financial year
So we do hedge 80% of the premium as per the policy.
As far as the impact is concerned, you are aware that SBI Life is going to be one of the least impacted company because of this.

adds.what: 14 new branches opened in the period
Over 72,000 agents added on a gross basis

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 individual rated premium growth of 14-15% and VoNB margin of 26-28%, though H1 IRP grew only about 12%; backing is partial (Q3 seasonality, a planned regular-pay deferred annuity, ULIP mix target, and 72,000 agent additions) with no specific capacity or contracted orders quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VoNB margin 27.9% in H1 (29.3% in Q2, 28.8% ex-GST) sits within the held 26-28% FY27 guide, and ~70bps of H1 YoY gain came from yield-curve movement that management says is partly passed to customers via non-par repricing in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Only 14 branches opened in H1 and 72,000 gross agent additions; no new plant-style capacity or dated capex was discussed, and growth is channel-driven rather than capacity-constrained.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 IRP growth guided at 14-15% versus about 12% in H1, so Q3 must accelerate sharply; individual APE grew 11% and agency Q2 growth slowed to about 6%, so delivery is not yet proven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief offers no utilisation figure for an insurer's capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated 14-15% IRP and 26-28% VoNB margin guidance and said it will stick to them, with no sign of raising them despite H1 IRP at about 12%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 IRP growth of about 12% is below the 14-15% full-year target, and the call gave no channel split to show how Q3 closes the gap; agency slowed to about 6% in Q2 and conservation fell to about 82% from 84%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to launch a regular-pay deferred annuity soon, possibly in Q3, at a margin similar to or above the company average.

rows.label: IRDAI distribution-economics guidelines
rows.why: Final guidelines are awaited; management sees SBI Life among the least impacted, but commission caps and differential pricing could hit banca and credit life economics, which are 53% of APE.

rows.label: IFRS 17 transition and ULIP CSM treatment
rows.why: Approach to be finalised by end-March 2027 with adoption from June 30, 2027, and an investor day planned before that; the ULIP CSM release treatment is still undisclosed.

rows.label: Continued non-par repricing
rows.why: Non-par was repriced in Q2 with yield benefits passed to customers, and management will keep repricing in Q3 and Q4, which supports non-par sales (guaranteed savings INR24.7bn, +27%) but may pressure margin.
